reproduction_is_host_dependent_not_code_.why_this_matters: a difference that appears on one x86 host and not another, at the same torch build and the same source, is a property of the CPU BLAS kernel dispatch on that machine and not of this renderer. the_right_invariant_at_the_intermediate_.answer: a NUMERIC TOLERANCE on cpu and bit-exactness on cuda -- which is what the harness already asserts
the_right_invariant_at_the_intermediate_.form: if dev == 'cuda': torch.equal(g, ref) else: max |g - ref| <= np.spacing(float32(max|ref|)) -- an assertion, not an exemption
the_right_invariant_at_the_intermediate_.why: the certified device is cuda and it is bitwise invariant at every width on every machine measured; the cpu stage has no consumer, and its residual is host-dependent at exactly one ulp, so a portable claim about it is a tolerance claim. check_batch_size_invariance continues to enforce the per-env, per-device property that actually gates certification.

the_stage.consumer: NONE. Nothing in the registry draws through nvdiff on device='cpu': PFRocketLanding raises on cpu by design and the six Mujoco locomotion nvdiff cells render through nvdiffrast on the card. The CPU path exists so the transform can be unit-tested without a GPU, which is what found this.
the_stage.mechanism: S4 has exactly four nonzeros per row, so every output element is a sum of four products whose accumulation order the kernel chooses by the dense operand's column count, 4*B. mvp_rows is NOT the cause: it has been matmul-free float64 since d1e61a1 and is bit-identical at every width on every machine measured.
